title: Win It, Score It
story: One player attacks a castle; if the guardian wins the ball, the guardian immediately attacks the opposite castle.
setup: Build two 10x15-yard fields with one mini goal at each end. Place two pairs at each field and spare balls beside the goals.
instructions: An attacker starts with the ball and tries to score in the far goal.
The defender protects the goal and may win the ball.
On a win, the defender attacks the opposite goal immediately.
The round ends with a goal or ball out; swap the starting role and restart quickly.
coach_lens: Notice whether defenders get between ball and goal, slow down near the attacker and recognize the instant they can attack. Praise recovery after being beaten.
questions: Where can you stand to protect the goal?
What is your first thought when you win the ball?

simplify: Start the defender one step farther away.
challenge: Use two small scoring gates at each end so players must scan.
low_attendance: Use one field and alternate pairs after every short round.
high_attendance: Duplicate fields; never form one long central line.
limited_equipment: Use cone gates and place spare balls safely outside the field.

safety: Use touch-tight defending without pushing or kicking through legs.
Keep waiting pairs beside, not behind, the goals.

diagram.alt: Two players face each other between opposite goals; arrows show either player counterattacking after winning the ball.

source.title: Trainingspraxis: Angreifen, Verteidigen und Umschalten
source.reviewer_notes: SmallSide-authored 1v1 transition game informed by DFB principles of small teams, goals, joy, intensity, repetition and immediate counterattack. German source reviewed; no wording or artwork translated or reproduced.
